headline: Approved moving elementary commissary kitchen to West High School and a $476,106.67 blue light alert system contract with TNT.
summary: Annual state financial reports and budget transfers were sent to the full board. A custodial contract with Aramark was tabled again so staff can bring back a revised proposal. The move of Beech Street modular classrooms to Manchester School of Technology was deferred.
decisions: Approved the September 9, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved the consent agenda as submitted, with all members present in favor.
Approved the Treasurer’s Report as submitted and sent it to the full board, 3-0.
Approved the $61,325.00 grants, gifts and donations report and set a public hearing on a $55,000 dog donation, 3-0.
Approved the Anthem Medicare Advantage plan for retirees over 65 for calendar year 2027, 3-0.
Approved $15,841.00 in city service invoices and sent them for board approval, 3-0.
Approved $38,637,967.88 in September 2026 expenditures and sent them for board approval, 3-0.
Approved $6,205.98 in professional leave requests, 3-0.
Approved indemnification contracts with six outside organizations, 3-0.
Approved the annual DOE and MS state financial reports and sent them to the board, 3-0.
Approved the fiscal 2026 closeout and fiscal 2027 financial reports and sent them to the full board, 3-0.
Approved FY26 and FY27 line item transfers and sent them to the board, 3-0.
Approved revisions to Policy Safety and Transportation 1009 on building and grounds trespassing, 3-0.
Approved repurposing $500,000 in FY26 CIP bus funds for six 10-passenger vans and one snow scraper, 3-0.
Approved TNT as vendor for the $476,106.67 Blue Light Alerting System, 3-0.
Deferred the Beech Street modular classroom move to Manchester School of Technology for discussion in nonpublic session.
Approved moving modular classrooms from Hillside and Southside to Jewett Street and Bakersville schools, 3-0.
Approved relocating and rebuilding the elementary school commissary kitchen at West High School, 2-1.
Re-tabled the Aramark custodial services contract, 3-0, pending a revised proposal.
Approved the First Student maintenance and storage agreement without Paragraph 3 and directed more talks on storage, 3-0.

MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE & FACILITIES 
 
October 21, 2026  7:00 p.m. 
 
1. Chairman O’Connell called the meeting to order at 6:45 p.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
 Present: Committee Members O’Connell, Parr and Stewart (Pro-Tem Member) 
 
Absent: Committee Members Turner and Hamer were absent. 
 
Chair O'Connell explained that the meeting, originally scheduled for October 14, 2026, had been 
postponed due to the lack of a quorum following the resignation of Committee Member Chris Potter 
and the unavailability of other Committee members.  Chair O'Connell also extended condolences to 
Committee Member Parr on the recent passing of his mother. A moment of silence was observed. 
 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
There were no individuals wishing to speak during public forum. 
 
4.  Approval of minutes from September 09, 2026, Finance & Facilities meeting.    
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee Member Stewart, it was moved 
to approve the minutes of the September 9, 2026 Finance and Facilities Meetings.  All were in favor 
and the motion passed.  
 
5. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
The Committee reviewed the Consent Agenda. No items were requested to be removed. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee Member Stewart, it was moved 
to approve the consent agenda as submitted.  All present were in favor and the motion passed.

6. ACTION AGENDA 
  
a. Annual DOE/MS Reports – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director    
of Finance   
 
1. DOE-25 for Fiscal 2026     
2.  MS-25 for Fiscal 2026     
3.  MS-24 for Fiscal 2027     
4.  MS-22 for Fiscal 2027     
5.  MS-26c for Fiscal 2027    
 
Executive Director of Finance Karen DeFrancis presented the District's annual financial reports, 
including the DOE-25, MS-25, MS-24, MS-22, and MS-26C.  Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the DOE-
25 reflects the District's fiscal year 2026 financial results, including revenues, expenditures, and fund 
balances. The report has been reconciled with the annual audit to date, with no significant adjustments 
anticipated. 
 
She highlighted several key financial results: 
 The general fund ended FY2026 with an unassigned fund balance of approximately $1.46 
million, which will be used to partially offset the FY2027 reduction in adequate education aid. 
 The food service fund balance was slightly more than $1 million, including approximately 
$892,000 reserved for cafeteria equipment replacement. 
 Special revenue funds had a year-end balance of approximately $474,000. 
 The District's expendable trust funds ended the fiscal year with approximately $10.7 million. 
 Total special education expenditures across all funding sources were approximately $72.9 
million, compared with $73.1 million the previous year. 
 The District's FY2026 cost per pupil was $18,919.02, representing a 4.3% increase over the 
prior year's $18,145.03.
October 14, 2026 October 21, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities – Postponed due to a lack of a quorum on 10/14/2026  
Page 5 of 27 
 
  
Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the MS reports provide financial information required by the New 
Hampshire Department of Revenue and are used in establishing the municipal tax rate.   
 
The MS-24 report reflected a $2.2 million reduction in anticipated adequate education aid for FY2027. 
Through the use of the prior-year fund balance and adjustments to projected Medicaid, interest, and 
other revenues, the District was able to offset most of the reduction. However, approximately $500,000 
remained to be supported through additional tax revenue. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Stewart requested clarification regarding the cost-per-pupil calculation and 
its comparability with other New Hampshire school districts. Mrs. DeFrancis explained that all 
districts follow the same state formula, although certain expenses, such as debt service, are 
excluded. Committee Member Stewart expressed interest in receiving comparative data to 
assist the Board and community in understanding the District's financial position. 
2. Committee Member Parr requested additional information regarding a separate $500,000 
reduction in anticipated special education aid. Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the original 
revenue estimate was based on the prior year's receipts, when the state reimbursement rate was 
approximately 92.1%. The current reimbursement rate was expected to be approximately 80%, 
resulting in lower anticipated revenues. 
3. The Committee also discussed the importance of using standardized state financial reports 
when comparing district expenditures, rather than simply dividing the total District budget by 
enrollment, as certain expenditures benefit students attending nonpublic schools. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis thanked Assistant Business Administrator Nick Bullard for his work preparing the 
reports and assisting with the annual audit. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee  Member Stewart, it was moved 
to approve the annual DOE and MS Reports, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee 
for approval. Committee Members O’Connell, Parr, and Stewart (Pro-Tem) were in favor.   
Committee Members Turner and Hamer were absent.  Motion passed.
October 14, 2026 October 21, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities – Postponed due to a lack of a quorum on 10/14/2026

b. Financial Reports – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance  
 
Mrs. Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance, presented the financial reports for the closeout 
of Fiscal Year 2026 and the beginning of Fiscal Year 2027. Mrs. DeFrancis referred Committee 
Members to page 119 of the agenda packet, explaining that the Fiscal Year 2026 expenditure report 
reconciled with the DOE-25 report previously reviewed by the Committee. She reported that General 
Fund expenditures exceeded the budget by approximately $9.6 million, requiring the use of expendable 
trust funds. Of that amount, $5.2 million had been anticipated and incorporated into the budget 
process. The remaining $4.4 million represented additional, unanticipated expenditures primarily 
associated with special education costs and health insurance claims that exceeded budgeted amounts. 
Regarding revenues, Mrs. DeFrancis reported that Fiscal Year 2026 revenues exceeded projections by 
approximately $2.4 million. These additional revenues resulted from higher-than-anticipated special 
education aid, interest earnings, Medicaid reimbursements, and tuition revenues.  Of that surplus, $1 
million was transferred into the Special Education Trust to help offset special education expenditures, 
while the remaining $1.4 million would be used to offset Fiscal Year 2027 adequate education aid. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis reviewed the expendable trust fund summary on page 120. She reported that the 
District began Fiscal Year 2026 with approximately $23 million in its trust funds.  During the fiscal 
year, the District utilized approximately $4.5 million from the trusts to support budgeted revenues, 
$5.2 million for anticipated expenditures, and an additional $4.4 million for unanticipated 
expenditures. These withdrawals were partially offset by the $1 million transfer from surplus revenues 
and approximately $900,000 in interest earnings.  As a result, the District ended Fiscal Year 2026 with 
a combined expendable trust fund balance of approximately $10.7 million as of June 30, 2026. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the Fiscal Year 2027 reports reflected expenditures and revenues 
through September and that it remained early in the fiscal year to determine final financial outcomes. 
 
She highlighted the following items: 
 General Fund Expenditures: Books, information resources, and equipment were projected to 
exceed budgeted amounts by approximately $1.5 million. The Board had previously approved 
using the Teaching and Learning Trust to offset these expenditures during the budget process.
October 14, 2026 October 21, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities – Postponed due to a lack of a quorum on 10/14/2026  
Page 7 of 27 
 
  
 Specialized Transportation: Current purchase orders reflected projected expenditures 
approximately $1.7 million above budget. Mrs. DeFrancis explained that this amount would be 
reduced through anticipated purchase-order adjustments and transportation billings. She noted 
that approximately $810,000 was billed during the prior fiscal year. Should similar billings 
occur this year, the remaining shortfall could be approximately $1 million. 
 Open Enrollment: The District would need to account for tuition expenses associated with 
students participating in open enrollment programs. Those expenditures would be incorporated 
into future financial reports once invoices were received. 
 General Fund Revenues: The District anticipated collecting all budgeted revenues. 
 Athletics: The District anticipated fully expending the athletic appropriation. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis reviewed the Food Service Fund reports on pages 125 and 126, noting that while the 
current projection reflected a break-even operating position, historical trends suggested that an 
additional transfer from the General Fund could become necessary. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis provided the following historical transfers: 
 Fiscal Year 2024: $825,000 
 Fiscal Year 2025: $600,000 
 Fiscal Year 2026: $685,000 
 
She clarified that these transfers were associated with the operational costs of the food service program 
and were not related to outstanding student meal debt.  She explained that although meal prices had 
increased, the additional revenue generated by the increase was relatively modest, approximately 
$50,000, and would be partially offset by increasing food and personnel expenses. Administration 
would continue monitoring the program and advise the Board if an additional transfer became 
necessary. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis reported that the District had approximately $18.7 million available in federal grant 
funding for Fiscal Year 2027. She explained that the majority of these funds were expected to be 
expended during the fiscal year, with some funding reserved for summer 2027 teacher salaries and 
anticipated carryover funding, primarily from Title I.  She also reviewed the Special Revenue Fund,

which includes donations and other grant funds, reporting a balance of approximately $519,000 as of 
the end of September. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Parr requested clarification regarding the District's special education 
expenditures, particularly the distinction between state reimbursement revenues and 
expenditures associated with contracted services and out-of-district tuition. Mrs. DeFrancis 
directed the Committee to page 119 and explained that professional services exceeded the 
budget by approximately $2.3 million, while tuition expenditures exceeded the budget by 
approximately $1.8 million. 
2. Dr. Parr noted that these categories included services needed to address staffing shortages, 
contracted personnel, and out-of-district placements. He asked for clarification regarding the 
District's total special education expenditures, including all funding sources.  Mrs. DeFrancis 
reported that total Fiscal Year 2026 special education expenditures were approximately $72.9 
million. 
3. Dr. Parr emphasized that the overall cost of providing special education services was 
significantly greater than the individual shortfalls discussed in the financial reports. He 
expressed concern that the public might not fully appreciate the extent to which special 
education expenses were supported through the local budget rather than state and federal 
funding.  Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the District receives special education funding from 
several sources, including state special education aid, Medicaid reimbursements, differentiated 
aid included in adequate education funding, and federal IDEA grants. However, she 
acknowledged that these funding sources do not come close to covering the District's total 
special education expenditures. 
4. Dr. Parr discussed the history of federal IDEA funding, noting that the originally contemplated 
federal contribution had never been fully realized. He emphasized that longstanding 
underfunding at both the state and federal levels continues to place substantial financial 
responsibility on local taxpayers. 
5. Committee Member Cindy Stewart expressed concern regarding the significant reduction in 
District trust fund balances.  She noted that the District ended Fiscal Year 2025 with 
approximately $23 million in trust funds but began Fiscal Year 2027 with only approximately 
$10.7 million, representing a reduction of more than $12 million in one year.  Drawing upon
October 14, 2026 October 21, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities – Postponed due to a lack of a quorum on 10/14/2026  
Page 9 of 27 
 
  
her professional experience in nonprofit development, Committee Member Stewart explained 
that trust funds are traditionally intended to preserve and grow principal while generating 
investment income to support future needs.  She expressed concern that the District had 
increasingly relied upon these funds to address operating budget shortfalls, rather than 
preserving them as long-term financial resources.  Committee Member Stewart emphasized that 
as the principal balances decrease, the District also loses the ability to generate the same level 
of interest income. She cautioned that the financial impact extends beyond the amount 
withdrawn because the District also sacrifices future investment earnings. 
6. Chairman O'Connell agreed with these concerns, noting that approximately two years earlier, 
trust fund balances were approximately $32 million. Those balances declined to approximately 
$23 million and subsequently to $10.7 million. 
7. Chairman O'Connell characterized this pattern of spending as unsustainable and expressed 
concern regarding both the depletion of principal and the corresponding reduction in 
investment earnings.  He connected these financial challenges to the District's ongoing special 
education obligations and the limited reimbursement received from state and federal sources. 
8. Chairman O'Connell also raised concerns regarding the financial implications of the state's 
open enrollment program.  He referenced approximately $240,000 in anticipated tuition costs 
associated with students attending Prospect Mountain through open enrollment and questioned 
how many of those students had previously attended Manchester public schools.  The 
Administration indicated that the information was not immediately available. 
9. Chairman O'Connell expressed concern that local property taxpayers could be required to fund 
tuition at another school district for students who may not have previously attended Manchester 
schools. 
10. Chairman O’Connell further expressed frustration with state education funding policies, 
including open enrollment and Education Freedom Account expenditures, particularly while 
the Manchester School District continues to experience financial pressures affecting staffing, 
student services, and educational programming. 
11. Chairman O'Connell also requested information regarding potential changes to Medicaid 
funding and whether reductions being discussed at the state level could affect the District's 
reimbursement revenues.  Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the District's Medicaid Coordinator, 
Nick D’Agostino, had projected revenues exceeding the amount originally budgeted for Fiscal 
Year 2027.  She reported that approximately $1 million in Medicaid reimbursements was

received during Fiscal Year 2026 and that the current year's estimate had increased from 
approximately $650,000 to $750,000.  Although she could not speak to the details of the 
anticipated state-level changes, Mrs. DeFrancis offered to have Mr. D’Agostino provide an 
additional presentation if requested.   
12. Chairman O'Connell acknowledged Mr. D’Agostino's work in improving the District's 
Medicaid reimbursement process and suggested that Administration continue monitoring 
potential funding changes. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee  Member Stewart, it was moved 
to approve the Financial Reports as presented and forward this item to the full Board of School 
Committee for approval. Committee Members O’Connell, Parr, and Stewart (Pro-Tem) were in favor.   
Committee Members Turner and Hamer were absent.  Motion passed. 
  
 
c. FY26 and FY27 Line Item Transfers – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive    
Director of Finance 
 
Executive Director of Finance Karen DeFrancis presented proposed line item transfers for fiscal years 
2026 and 2027.  Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the FY2026 general fund transfers were necessary to 
reconcile final expenditures and adjust individual accounts that exceeded their budgeted amounts. The 
transfers involve moving available appropriations between accounts and do not increase overall 
expenditures.  An additional FY2026 transfer of $685,000 from the General Fund to the Food Service 
Fund was presented to address the previously discussed operational shortfall. 
 
For FY2027, Mrs. DeFrancis requested a transfer associated with the District's custodial services 
agreement with Aramark. She explained that, historically, the City's Department of Public Works paid 
Aramark, and the School District reimbursed the City through its municipal services account. Effective 
July 1, 2026, the District began paying Aramark directly.  As a result, funding must be transferred 
from the City Services account to the District's Repairs and Maintenance account. Mrs. DeFrancis 
emphasized that this was an accounting adjustment and would not affect the District's overall budget. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Stewart, duly seconded by Committee  Member Parr, it was moved 
to approve the 2026 and 2027 Line Item Transfers, and forward this item to the Board of School
October 14, 2026 October 21, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities – Postponed due to a lack of a quorum on 10/14/2026  
Page 11 of 27 
 
  
Committee for approval. Committee Members O’Connell, Parr, and Stewart (Pro-Tem) were in favor.  
Committee Members Turner and Hamer were absent.  Motion passed. 
 
d. Safety and Transportation 1009:  Buildings and Grounds Security –     
Trespassing – by Matthew Upton, Executive Director of Legal and Policy 
 
Executive Director of Legal and Policy, Attorney Matt Upton, presented proposed revisions to Policy 
Safety and Transportation 1009, Building and Grounds Security/Trespassing, to bring the District into 
compliance with recent changes to New Hampshire law.  Attorney Upton explained that the amended 
law requires the governing body of a school district to either issue no-trespass orders itself or formally 
designate an entity to issue such orders on its behalf.  Historically, the Superintendent has coordinated 
with the Manchester Police Department regarding the issuance of no-trespass orders. The proposed 
revisions would formally designate the Manchester Police Department as the entity authorized to issue 
these orders on behalf of the Board of School Committee, with the Superintendent serving as the 
administrative liaison. 
 
Attorney Upton indicated that the proposed language had been developed in consultation with the 
Manchester Police Department and the City Solicitor's Office.  He further explained that an individual 
receiving a no-trespass order has the right to appeal the decision to the Board of School Committee 
within ten days. If an appeal is filed, the Board must provide the individual an opportunity to be heard 
at its next regularly scheduled meeting. 
 
Attorney Upton recommended approval of the proposed revisions to ensure compliance with the 
statutory requirements. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Stewart, duly seconded by Committee  Member Parr, it was moved 
to approve the revisions to policy Safety and Transportation 1009: Buildings and Grounds Security – 
Trespassing, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee for approval. Committee 
Members O’Connell, Parr, and Stewart (Pro-Tem) were in favor.  Committee Members Turner and 
Hamer were absent.  Motion passed.

e. Reallocation of CIP Monies – by Dr. Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent of High 
Schools and Operations 
 
Dr. Espinola presented a request to reallocate $500,000 in previously approved FY2026 transportation-
related bonded funding.  She explained that the District had originally received approval for $1.2 
million in transportation capital expenditures, consisting of $700,000 for the replacement of six school 
buses and $500,000 for the purchase of five additional buses to expand the District's fleet.  Due to the 
ongoing shortage of qualified bus drivers and the need for more flexible transportation options, the 
Administration requested permission to repurpose the $500,000 designated for fleet expansion to 
purchase six 10-passenger vans and snow-removal equipment for the District's buses. 
 
Dr. Espinola explained that smaller vans would allow the District to transport athletic teams and other 
small student groups without requiring a full-size school bus and CDL driver. This would help 
preserve the existing bus fleet and available drivers for regular student transportation routes.  The 
estimated purchase price for six vans was between $330,000 and $390,000. Including initial insurance, 
registration, and equipment expenses, the anticipated first-year cost was approximately $354,000 to 
$438,000. For planning purposes, the Administration proposed using approximately $425,000, leaving 
an estimated $75,000 for a snow scraper and other eligible expenses. 
 
Dr. Espinola also explained that the snow-removal equipment would be a long-term District asset, 
initially used where buses are currently housed and eventually relocated to Manchester when 
transportation operations return to the city. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Parr expressed support for the request, particularly the purchase of smaller 
vehicles for athletic transportation, which had previously been discussed by the Committee on 
Athletics.  He questioned whether the remaining $700,000 designated for bus replacement was
